summary: NASA welcomed Côte d’Ivoire as the newest signatory to the Artemis Accords, expanding international alignment on space exploration, while a joint U.S.-India satellite captured time-lapse video of a volcanic eruption. In military space, the United Kingdom established its first space squadron aimed at protecting satellites and countering adversary threats, as the U.S. Air Force and Space Force accelerated research into orbital cargo delivery, and reports indicated SpaceX gained unique access to classified Department of Defense space tracking data. In the commercial sector, satellite startup Hubble Network raised $200 million in Series C funding, Vast announced a dedicated Lunar Programs Division, and Outpost unveiled a new in-space manufacturing service. Human spaceflight developments saw NASA assign crew members to the SpaceX Crew-14 mission to the International Space Station while preparing to conduct human health and performance studies during Crew-13. Scientific findings included observations from the James Webb Space Telescope showing early galaxies seeding the universe with heavy elements, alongside research suggesting samples from the asteroid Bennu share an origin linked to Jupiter. Looking ahead, readers should watch for the launch of Starfish Space’s first operational Otter spacecraft into orbit next month.
